subject: Confidential: Hosting recommendation & GPU sizing for Cardinal pilot
body:
From: Sam Rivera <sam.rivera@cardinalhealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Menon <priya.menon@cardinalhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: (Confidential) hosting posture + sizing ask for pilot

Mina / Redwood team,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We need a short write-up comparing a Private (VPC/on-prem handshake) deployment vs Redwood Dedicated reserved capacity for our upcoming NLP pilot that will process PHI and must meet our audit controls. Key asks:
- Clear recommendation for pilot (12 weeks) and production (SLA-backed)
- GPU slate and sizing (expected concurrency ~40 requests/min, average seq len 350 tokens)
- Minimum compliance evidence (SOC2, access logs, key management options)
- Cost delta and uplift for isolation

Can you get something over by EOD Monday?

—Sam
Sr. Product, Cardinal Health

---

On Thu, Nov 4, 2027 at 10:05 AM Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com> wrote:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Sam Rivera <sam.rivera@cardinalhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Nov 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: (Confidential) hosting posture + sizing ask for pilot

Sam — thanks for the clear list. High-level recommendation up front: for a 12-week pilot that must process PHI and demonstrate auditability, we recommend starting with a Private deployment in your VPC (private control plane) for the pilot, then evaluate swapping to Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) for production if you prioritize lower unit cost over data-plane control.

Why Private for pilot (short bullets):
- Full network isolation and customer-managed KMS (meets typical PHI controls)
- Easier to satisfy procurement/audit ask quickly — no shared tenancy questions
- We can mirror the production topology and provide audit logs early

Sizing (pilot - recommended):
- Baseline throughput target: 40 requests/min with p95 latency <= 600ms at 350 token average
- Suggested GPU slate: 4 x H100-80GB (NVL) or H100-equivalent instances optimized for FP16/INT8 execution
- Concurrency plan: 8 worker processes with dynamic batching; target batch size ~64 for cost/latency balance
- KV cache: enable prefix caching to reduce repeated context cost by ~30% for conversational flows

Production (if move to Dedicated reserved):
- Start commit: 8 GPUs (H100) for predictable throughput; autoscale with burst capacity to 12 GPUs for peak windows
- Throughput estimate: 200k tokens/min steady state (depending on model variant)

Compliance evidence we will deliver:
- SOC2 summary & controls map (attached)
- Audit log export template & retention policy (can be extended to 7 years on Private)
- Network checklist for on-prem/airgap installs (attached)

Costs: loosely, pilot Private (managed in your VPC) runs ~1.4–1.8x the Dedicated-per-token cost due to isolation ops and smaller GPU footprint. We'll run a detailed cost model once we have expected token volumes.

Next steps / asks from Sam:
1) Confirm whether procurement needs an on-prem air-gapped deployment or if VPC private control plane is sufficient.
2) Share expected monthly token volume range for the pilot (low/nominal/high).
3) Approve a quick joint SOC2 controls review session (30m).

I attached a draft GPU slate and our SOC2 summary. Karthik — adding you for quant/latency notes. Marissa / Vivek — pricing and credit ask below.

Best,
Mina
Director, Solutions (Redwood Inference)

Attachments: Cardinal_GPU_Slate_v2.xlsx; SOC2_Audit_Summary_2026.pdf; private-deploy-network-checklist.docx

On Thu, 4 Nov 2027 at 11:22 AM Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com> wrote:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Sam Rivera <sam.rivera@cardinalhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Nov 2027 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: (Confidential) hosting posture + sizing ask for pilot

Sam — quick technical clarifications to the sizing note:
- Model variant: assume a 13B assistant-style decoder (often our default for PHI redaction + summarization). If you use a 70B encoder-decoder family the GPU count will ~2–3x.
- H100 vs A100: H100 gives ~1.6x throughput for FP16 inference; if procurement restricts to older cards, we can run a mixed fleet but need an escape hatch for performance SLAs.
- Quantization: INT8 will reduce memory pressure and allow larger batches; we recommend a quantized 13B for pilot unless you require exact float fidelity.
- KV cache sizing: for 350-token averages, plan for ~4GB KV per concurrent worker (varies by model).

Operational notes:
- On Private, we instrument detailed token-level billing and request tracing.
- For Dedicated, we can provide tenant isolation at the runtime layer but not physical isolation; this influences some audit language.

I'll run a quick perf sim today with the 13B quantized profile and share numbers.
